ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \angle ACD=90^\circ$, $ \angle D=15^\circ$, point B is on the perpendicular bisector of $ AD$, if $ AC=4$, then what is the length of $ AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point B is on the perpendicular bisector of $AD$,\\
it follows that $AB=BD$,\\
thus, $\angle BAD=\angle D=15^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle ABC=\angle BAD+\angle D=30^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ACD=90^\circ$ and $AC=4$,\\
it follows that $AB=2AC=\boxed{8}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: As can be seen from the attached figure, A is at the upper left, C is at the lower left, B and D are located on the same horizontal straight line, and the order is C, B, D; AC is a vertical line segment, CD is the horizontal base, and a right angle is marked at C, indicating AC ⟂ CD; from A connect respectively to B and D, forming line segments AB and AD. Reasoning: Because the problem statement gives that B is on the perpendicular bisector of AD, the distances from B to A and D are equal, that is, AB=BD. Therefore triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, with base AD, so ∠BAD=∠ADB. Also because C, B, D are collinear, ∠ADB is the ∠D=15° in the problem, so ∠BAD=15°. In triangle ABD, ∠ABD=180°-15°-15°=150°. Since BC and BD are opposite rays, ∠ABC is the adjacent supplementary angle of ∠ABD, ∠ABC=180°-150°=30°, that is, ∠ABC=∠BAD+∠D=30°. In right triangle ABC, ∠ACB=90°, ∠ABC=30°, AC=4, and AC is the right-angle side opposite the 30° angle, AB is the hypotenuse. In a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, the hypotenuse is equal to 2 times the side opposite the 30° angle, therefore AB=2AC=2×4=8.
